name: Jjak-mat-chu-gi
description: Jjak-mat-chu-gi (짝맞추기 - 'Making Pairs') is a traditional Korean domino game played with Gol-pae (bone tiles). Unlike Western dominoes where players match end-to-end, this is a 'pair-making' game where the objective is to form specific combinations (Civil and Military pairs). It is a draw-and-discard game similar in structure to Rummy but played with tiles.

content.text: Jjak-mat-chu-gi (짝맞추기 - 'Making Pairs') is a traditional Korean domino game played with Gol-pae (bone tiles). Unlike Western dominoes where players match end-to-end, this is a 'pair-making' game where the objective is to form specific combinations (Civil and Military pairs). It is a draw-and-discard game similar in structure to Rummy but played with tiles.
Dates back centuries in Korea, adapted from Chinese domino sets. It was first documented in Western literature by Stewart Culin in 1895 in his book 'Korean Games'.
32 tiles: 11 'Civil' pairs (matching) and 10 'Military' tiles (unique, paired by total spots).

First player draws 6 tiles, others 5 each. Remaining tiles form a face-down reserve. First player is chosen by draw (tile 2-5 or highest spots plays first).

items.text: Win only by reserve: A player's third (winning) pair can only be made by matching a tile drawn from the reserve; winning by taking a discard is not allowed.
Row draw: Shuffled tiles are placed in a row; tiles are drawn from one end of the row instead of a reserve pile.
Alternative military pairing: Some sources use a different grouping for Military pairs: e.g. 2-6 with 3-6, 2-5 with 3-5, 2-4 with 3-4, 1-4 with 2-3, 1-2 with 4-5.
